name: Yam Scale (Tuber Scale)
description: A scale insect infestation of yam tubers, both in the field and during storage. Scales appear as small white or brown circular discs on the tuber surface, causing weight loss, shriveling, and reduced market value.
symptoms: Small white to brown circular scales on tuber surface
Scales firmly attached to tuber skin
Tubers becoming unmarketable in heavy infestations
causes: Infested seed yams used for planting
Poor storage conditions with low ventilation
Spread through infested soil and field debris
treatments: Dip infested seed yams in insecticide solution (e.g., chlorpyrifos) before planting
Scrub tubers gently in water to remove scales before storage
Apply vegetable oil emulsion (2% neem oil) to stored tubers
prevention: Treat seed yams with neem extract before planting
Maintain good ventilation in storage structures
Inspect and remove infested tubers from storage regularly
Practice field rotation to reduce soil populations
